findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant to the left of the dish machine to be damaged. The PIC was informed and plans to submit a work order for repair. Ensure this repair is complete prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed floor underneath fryer to be soiled with grease and food debris. Clean floor underneath fryer.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed in-use wiping cloth to be stored on counter top in kitchen. Store in-use wiping cloths in chemical sanitizer solution in-between uses. Towel was removed and place in laundry container during inspection.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed lighting in walk-in cooler to be insufficient. Area in rear of walk-in cooler near walk-in freezer door is very dark. Add an additional light source to this area. 

6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: Observed interior cavity of microwave in kitchen to be soiled with food splash. Clean and sanitize interior cavity of microwave. (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to have spatulas in the drawer with cracks and pits in the rubber. Also, the salad bar and the hot holding table have plexiglass shields that do not appear to be easily cleanable. The screws in the plexiglass guard on the steam table are rusting. New spatulas are going to be ordered and the guards on the hot and cold serving table units are going to be addressed.

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed paint in the lower left side corner of the men’s restroom next to the toilet to have peeling paint. Seal the wall so that it is not absorbent. 6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Food thermometers were stored in a container with single use thermometer probe wipes, a mustard packet, markers, pens, tape, and other items. Probes of food thermometers were uncovered and not in cases. Food thermometers were relocated to a separate container. Ensure proper storage of food thermometers between uses.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: See inspection report from 5/18/21 for details.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC (interim certified dietary manager) at time of inspection did not have proof of a current CFM. PIC noted he took a manager certification at one time but did not have a copy with him. PIC was advised that proof of current manager certification was required and to consider carrying a wallet card with him to provide certification in the future.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee prepared a sani-bucket and then proceeded to put clean dishes away without a hand wash in between. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and was observed washing hands as needed between tasks throughout the remainder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 Rinse gauge of dish machine was observed reading up to and above 200F during final rinse cycle. Rinse water temperature as it enters the manifold was discussed. PIC called for service during inspection (see general comments for additional information). Ensure adjustments/repairs result in the final rinse at the manifold being not less than 180F and not more than 194F, and the surface temperature at the dish rack during ware washing cycle being at least 160F.
In a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Bottom inside ice scoop holder was soiled with general buildup. Ice scoop holder and scoops were cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection. Ensure ice scoop holder and scoops are cleaned daily/as needed.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in clean, protected location if utensils, such as ice scoops, are used for a non-TCS food.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 PIC was unable to provide an irreversible registering temperature indicator. PIC was advised on the need for dish machine test strips or some type of maximum registering thermometer for the purpose of verifying the final rinse temperature at the surface of dishes. PIC contacted supplier during inspection and ordered test strips. (see general comments for additional information).
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Sani-bucket at the front service line had murky water in it. Solution appeared to be left from use during a previous shift. PIC tested the solution to confirm a concentration of 0ppm quat. Proper disposal of waste water after use was discussed. Old sanitizer solution was discarded during the inspection.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of used sanitizer solutions after they are no longer needed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112  (Pf) Hot water sanitizing rinse at dish machine is less than 180°F. Maximum registering thermometer reads 155F. Repair unit so that hot water rinse is maintained between 180°F to 194°F. Reference 4-501.112. Sanitizing is going to occur in the 3 part sink. Dishes will be washed in the machine and taken to the 3 part for chemical sanitizing according to the manufacturer specifications of the sanitizer used.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text: 4-203.12  (Pf) Ambient air/water thermometer in dish machine is not accurate. Must be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. Reference 4-203.12. Observed the dish machine thermometer on the wash cycle to read between 190F and 200F. Inspector thermometer reads 155F. Dish surfaces shall be 160F for proper sanitizing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly. Observed the clean utensils to be stored in containers with crumbs and debris in the bottoms. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Utensils and containers were placed at dish.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13  (Pf) An irreversible registering temperature indicator is not provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature in the mechanical ware washing machine. Employee is not able to verify if the hot water is properly sanitizing. Provide appropriate hot water temperature-sensitive tape or paper thermometers. Reference 4-302.13. Provide thermometer as described above.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540. Upon arrival there were no certified food managers in charge of the kitchen. The food manager returend. He stated that they will get more individuals manager certified.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: 6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by a rolling garbage can in the dish room. The can was moved. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly in a bucket at the clean utensil shelved and on a soiled hook at the prep table in back. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Bucket with utensils and hook with whisk were all taken to the back and properly washed, rinsed and sanitized.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the edges of equipment in difficult to reach areas, dust on salad bar cooler condenser fan and handles of faucet. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13. Clean areas of the tables and areas around legs of equipment more thoroughly.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text: 5-103.12 (Pf) A water supply under pressure is not available at the hand sink next to the ice machine and a leak of water is observed at the hand sink at the salad bar area. Water under pressure must be provided to all fixtures and equipment requiring water connections to operate. Install/repair water supply.  Reference 5-103.12.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed sausage patties in the walk in cooler with a temperature of 91F and a time of 8am. The cook states that the food was cooked at 8am but put into the walk in to cool after breakfast just a few minutes before we arrived. We arrived at approximately 9:30am. The sausage will be remarked with the appropriate time for cooling record. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling sausage patties is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed dust build up on the pass through cooler air intake. Clean and maintain free of dust accumulation. this will also help the unit to maintain proper temperature. 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the cooler air condenser on the top of the pass through unit.  Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Observed the floor and wall under the hand sink at the serving area out front to be soiled. Also general floors in the facility have soil accumulation that appears to be more than just from this morning. Make sure to clean floors properly on a daly basis so that soil does not accumulate. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Area above pass through hot box and cooler is soiled with dust. Clean and maintain free of dust. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the handle of a knife clean in the block to have soil up next to the hilt where the handle is connected. The knife was pulled for proper cleaning. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time it may have become contaminated.  Do not put away soiled items. Check items carefully that come from dish.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed a cart in the dish room where mops are hanging and the mop sink is located to be soiled with food debris. Clan and keep clean. Clean all transport carts on a regular basis and any time thy get soiled. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean forks and plates to be on a cart in the area where soiled mops are hanging and the mop sink is located. Cover the utensils and invert the plates when placed on a cart for transport to the floor. Also, avoid storing them in this area as splash and cleaning equipment is not considered a clean area. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The floor to the left of the door to the dining room from the kitchen and to the right of the dining room door behind the ice machine are soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.  750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Observed a used Gatorade bottle to be filled with milk and chocolate stored in the stainless reach in cooler laying on its side on top of string cheese and crackers. Personal food shall be stored separated from food for service at the facility to protect that food from potential outside sources of contamination. Bottle of what appeared to be chocolate milk was discard. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: Observed an employee to walk around the kitchen drinking a bottle of water. Eating and drinking shall take place in designated areas. Not in kitchen or food prep areas. Employee finished bottle of water and discarded bottle. 750-530e Employees shall maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness and shall conform to good hygienic practices during all working periods in the food service establishment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Hot line lids and area around hot line is soiled with accumulated food debris.  The area was cleaned. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140(b) Observed spaghetti sauce and noodles with an internal temp of 102 F cooling in the walk in cooler with  no time labeling. Food employees shall label the time food began cooling to ensure food is reaching appropriate cooling milestones (135 F to 70 F in 2 hours and 70 F to 41 F in 4 hours). A time label was added to correct violation.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-140 Observed the single door reach in cooler adjacent to the prep table to have an internal air temp of approximately 50 F. A container of yogurt stored in the unit was probed and had an internal temp of 44.9 F. TCS foods from this unit were moved to the walk in cooler. Cold holding units shall be able to maintain food temperatures at 41 F or below.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed a cutting board stored ready for use underneath a prep table to be soiled with an accumulation of a black substance. Cutting board was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Clean and maintain food contact surfaces to prevent potential contamination of food.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 (1) Observed the floor underneath large equipment such as the service line, reach in coolers, ice machine, and under the shelving in the dry storage to be soiled with an accumulation of dust and food debris. (2) Observed the floor drain under the ice machine to be missing its cover. Provide a cover. (3) Observed the floor drain underneath the can opener in the prep area to be soiled with a stick residue. Clean and maintain floors and floor drains to prevent providing food, water, and harborage for pests.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed a spray bottle of chemical used for cleaning (orange force) stored intermingled with cutting boards and food on the shelving below the prep table by the cook line. Chemicals shall be stored in a manner to prevent potential chemical contamination of food or food equipment. Store chemicals below and away from food and food equipment. Spray bottle was removed to correct the violation.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
REPEAT
Observed cut cantaloupe and honey dew on the breakfast bar at 58F. The cut melon was discarded. Do not store foods above the pan fill line on the serving bar. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage, service, display (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non food contact items to be soiled: 1) knife holder on wall 2) seals on upright stainless cooler 3) bottom of hot holding box 4) area around serving bar 5) single service utinesil holders. Wednesday is a cleaning day according to the employee. Some areas may need to be wiped on a more regular basis to maintian absence of food debris accmulation as these are repeat violaitons.  750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The floors in the facility kitchen around the legs of the equipment have an accumulation of soil.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors maintain clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed cantalopue at 44.6F on the salad bar. Top half was warmer. Toward the bottom fruit was 40F.  All fruit was discarded. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Watch placement of sweet fruits such as cantalopue that are potentially hazardous/tcs foods. Do not leave any gaps in the cold holding bar.  Make certian that items like this are pre chilled.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed some areas where there is a good amount of food crumbs dust and debris such as: 1) the bottom shelf of prep across from the ovens (cleaned) 2) the tops of bulk bins 3) hot holding cabinet 4) ice dispenser drip tray 5) outsides of single service dispensers.  4750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed containers holding clean crooking utensils to be soiled in the bottoms with food debris and dust. Clean containers holding clean utensils and maintain free of accumulated soil. 
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: The hand sink next to the door leading to the cafeteria is leaking. 750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code. Repair leak

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: Employee men's restroom does not have hand towels. 750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory. Provide towels.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Personal drink (open bottle of water) was observed on the top shelf in the reach-in freezer. Bottle was removed from the area.

Employees may drink from closed beverage containers if the containers are handled to prevent contamination of the employee's hands; the containers; and exposed food, equipment, utensils and other items. Provide a designated storage area for personal food/beverages away from/below products served to clients.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Several sani-buckets tested below 150ppm quat, and the effective concentration for the sanitizer in use is 150-400ppm. Solutions were remade to be at proper concentration (2000ppm).

Maintain quat solutions in sani-buckets at 200ppm. Change solutions as needed throughout the operating day, and use test strips to verify concentration is correct. Let the solution run through the line for several seconds prior to filling buckets and bottles, and make sure air bubbles are not interfering with dispensing of chemical.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) wall mounted knife rack (dust/debris on top) - rack and knives taken to dish area during inspection;  and
B) ice dispenser shoot on front service line (lime buildup).

Clean and sanitize food contact between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
7500.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) bottom inside reach-in freezer (food crumbs);
B) inside hotbox on front line (shelving and bottom with splash);   and
C) metal shelving at front service line (dust/debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Serving utensils were observed in soiled storage containers in the prep area and at the front service line. The bottom inside containers had varying degrees of splash and/or debris. All utensils and storage containers were taken to the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized.

Cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Maintain storage containers clean.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water had very low pressure at the handsink by the tray return in the dish room. Provide adequate water pressure at the handsink.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Metal drain pan under the front counter service line was soiled with mold buildup, and the floor under/around the metal pan was also soiled with general buildup. Clean the metal drain pan, the drain line above the pan, and the floor under/around the metal pan daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and general debris.

Floors and drains shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Tray of cookies on top of bakers rack did not have overhead cover. The very top of the rack was not covered with a pan or baking sheet. Trays of cookies were done cooling and were covered with plastic wrap.
NOTE: Uncovered trays of product below other trays on a bakers rack are considered covered. Make sure an overhead cover is provided for uncovered trays of product stored on the top rungs of the rack.

B) Plastic wrap on a pan of seasoning on spice storage table was torn. Replace the plastic wrap daily, and keep foods covered between uses/during long-term (overnight) storage.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop holder had buildup of debris and a water bottle cap in the bottom. Scoops and holder were placed through a ware washing cycle in the dish machine.

Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handles extended out of is.
Clean the ice scoop holder daily/as needed, and maintain it clean.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
750.830f - Knives and spreaders in a storage rack had food debris stuck on them. Also, a serving utensil had stuck on food debris in clean utensil storage area. The storage rack and all utensils were taken to the dish area to go through ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation. Repeat the process of as many times as necessary to remove debris and ensure all surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets tested at 0ppm and less than 100ppm quat in the prep areas. Manager was unsure but the solutions appeared to be leftover from the previous operating evening. Solutions were emptied and remade at proper concentration (200ppm).

Maintain quat solutions in sani-buckets at 200ppm. Change solutions as needed throughout the operating day, and use test strips to verify concentration is correct. At the end of operations daily, empty solutions and do not leave old solutions out for potential use the next day.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - A) Can opener blade had food debris on it. An accumulation of metal shavings was also noted around the blade. The can opener was cleaned/sanitized during the inspection.
Clean and sanitize the can opener and the holder between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

B) Both ends of the dish machine had an accumulation of dust and debris/splash in the areas in front of/around the plastic curtains. Plastic curtains on the dirty dish side were also soiled.
Clean and sanitize the dish machine curtains and the areas in front of/around the curtains daily/as needed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Serving utensils were observed in a soiled storage pan. The bottom inside the pan had a buildup of grease and food debris. All utensils and the storage pan were taken to the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized.

Cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Maintain storage containers clean.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 & 1100 - A) Plumbing had a leak under the basin of the handsink by chemical storage shelves. Water was flowing from the sink along the floor to a nearby floor drain. Manager stated a work order has been placed.  

B) Drain cup under the single basin prep sink was loose and water was observed flowing across the floor as a result. Drain cup was repositioned to minimize the issue. 

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.
Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120  - A) Paper towels were not available at the handsinks in the dish area. Paper towels were provided.

Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Also, have extra stock available for staff to restock as needed throughout operations. 

B) Handsinks throughout had varying degrees of splash and buildup in the basins and along edges.

Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of splash/debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Baseboard was loose along the wall beneath the front counter hand soap dispenser. Re-seal the baseboard in this area.

B) Metal drain pan under the front counter service line was soiled with mold buildup. Clean the metal drain pan and the drain line above the pan daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

C) Floors were soiled with food and/or general buildup of debris in the following areas:
1. under front service counter;
2. under ice machine;   and
3. under all cooking equipment.
Clean floors under equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

D) Floor drain under single basin prep sink was soiled with grimy buildup/mold. Clean the floor drain under the prep sink, and maintain it clean.

Floors, including drains, shall be kept clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.140b - Beef stew leftover from lunch observed in walkin cooler #2 had surface and internal temperatures between 64F-74F. Time was not marked on the plastic wrap. Manager noted the product was pulled and began cooling on an ice bath around 130p. The time was placed on the plastic wrap. The plastic wrap was left off part of the pan to allow heat to vent off while the stew was cooling. A pan of ice was placed under the beef stew and the product was stirred to finish dropping the product to 70F/below within the 2hr time frame. 

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled with the date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F/below. **The cooling process begins when foods reach 135F. The only way to know the temperature if to monitor it with a clean, calibrated stem thermometer. Keep track of the time and temperature during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures within the designated time frame for proper cooling (135F to 70F/below w/in 2 hrs; 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4hrs - total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs).

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Boxes of ice cream were observed on the floor in the walkin freezer. Boxes of food were placed on shelving during the inspection.

Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop holder was observed to have buildup of debris in the bottom. Ice scoops and holder were placed through a ware washing cycle in the dish machine.
Clean the holder and scoops as needed to eliminate buildup of debris/protect scoops and ice from potential cross contamination.

Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handles extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle labeled Multi-Quat tested at 0ppm. Solution was emptied, bottle and spray nozzle were rinsed, and solution was refilled from the wall mounted chemical dispenser in the dish room. Sanitizer was observed at 200ppm quat after foam settled and solution was checked again.

Maintain sani-buckets and spray bottles of sanitizer at the proper range indicated on EcoLab directional sheet (150-400ppm). Use test strips to verify solution is at proper sanitizing concentrations. If spray bottles are maintained, check the concentration daily to verify the sanitizer has not worn down below effective range for proper sanitizing. Also, use paper towels with spray bottles and discard after use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) Wall behind/below dish machine on dirty dish side was soiled with black mold. 
B) Mold growth was starting to accumulate on the south wall in walkin cooler #1.

Clean walls as needed, and maintain clean.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
750160 & 280 - Styrofoam cup was observed inside bacon bits. Cup was removed and discarded by Kitchen Manager.

Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. When handling and dispensing ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Metal server and serving spoon in clean utensil storage area were soiled with stuck on food debris. Utensils were taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation. Repeat the process as many times as needed in order to ensure all debris is removed and all surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Pans used for storage of clean utensils were soiled with splash and food debris. Clean storage containers as needed and maintain clean. Provide covers if possible to help minimize buildup of splash and debris. Pans and utensils were taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

B) Tongs were observed with food surfaces extended up out of container. Store cleaned/sanitized utensils with handles presented out so food contact surfaces will not be touched when utensils are retrieved for use. Tongs and container were taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

Cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 - (R) Tiles adjacent to floor drain and around electrical outlets beneath the ice machine table on front service line are loose from prior water damage. Replace loose tiles and re-seal the floor under the ice machine table.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Employee drink was observed on a shelf in the prep area with food trays. Drink was moved to the manager's office for storage.

Employees shall consume food/drinks only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food/drinks there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket on cook line was less than 100ppm quat. Solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Change buckets every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Let the solution run through the line for several seconds prior to filling buckets, and use test strips to verify solution is at proper concentration. When checking the sanitizer concentration make sure the foam settles out and only the liquid is being tested in order to obtain a more accurate result.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1100 - Drain line from ice machine on front service line is not properly aligned with the floor drain beneath. During the inspection today water was observed dripping on to the edge of the floor drain cover and on the edge of the adjacent floor tile. Kitchen Manager noted the line is mobile (ice machine table can be moved for cleaning, etc.), and the drain line doesn't always get right over the floor drain at times. 
Reposition the drain line so it drips in the floor drain and not on the edge/adjacent tiles around the drain.

Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Tiles adjacent to floor drain and around electrical outlets beneath the ice machine table on front service line are loose and have moisture accumulation underneath (resulted over time from ice machine drain line leaking on the floor - see #29). When pressure was added to tiles murky, brown water came to the surface. The tiles themselves are also soiled with debris, moisture, and what appeared to be mold in at least one area.
Replace loose tiles and re-seal the floor under the ice machine table.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - BBQ chicken cooling in walkin cooler #2 was dated but did not have time indicated on the label. Manager noted the cooling process began around 1:15p when the product was pulled from the steam table and placed on an ice bath. Temperatures were checked around 2:55p. Surface temperature was 66F, and internal temperature was 73F-74F. Plastic wrap was removed and pan of ice was placed under chicken in the walkin cooler to help finish rapidly cooling the product. Internal temperature was checked again by Manager around 3:45p; product was at 44F.
 
Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. It is ok to leave cooling foods uncovered in the walkin cooler as long as the shelving above is clean and no raw products (raw meats and/or unwashed produce) are stored above the cooling foods. Monitor the time and temperature during the cooing process to ensure products are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame: 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs).

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
A) Ice scoop holder was soiled with buildup in the bottom. Ice scoop holder and all ice scoops were placed through ware washing process.
Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

B) Styrofoam bowl was observed inside shredded cheese at the front line cooler. Bowl was removed and discarded.
To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees. Use scoops with handles for dispensing foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution was at 0ppm quat in all buckets. Dispenser was checked to verify sanitizer was dispensing properly. Buckets were remade with solution at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Change buckets every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Let the solution run through the line for several seconds prior to filling buckets, and use test strips to verify solution is at proper concentration.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Carry out boxes and plates were observed with food surfaces stored up at the front service line. Boxes and plates were inverted.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects them from potential contamination. Store items so food contact surfaces are covered or inverted.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Spaghetti sauce in walkin cooler #2 had a prep date of 5/7 and should have been used or discarded by the end of operations on 5/13. Manager discarded the spaghetti sauce.
Refrigerated, potentially hazardous food shall be clearly dated and consumed or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap and paper towels were not available in the women's employee restroom. Soap and paper towel dispensers were filled during the inspection. 
Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels in restrooms and at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Have a backup supply of soap and paper towels available for use between services from housekeeping.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Sausage links in walkin cooler that were cooling from breakfast did not have a time stamp on the plastic wrap. Sausages had internal temperatures at 58F-60F. Assistant Manager noted the sausages were pulled to begin cooling around 9:30-9:45a. Facility still had plenty of time for sausages to finish reaching 41F. Management was advised after using ice baths to start cooling process to loosely wrap cooling foods when placed in walkin and label with date and time.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.280 & 290 - A) Yellow bowl was observed as scoop in bulk sugar bin. Bowl was removed by Kitchen Manager. Scoops with handles shall be used for dispensing foods. B) Blue ice scoop holder had buildup in the bottom. Holder and ice scoops were ran through ware washing process during the inspection. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Maintain ice scoop holders clean.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - A full jug of quat sanitizer was present at the 3 part sink, but it was not dispensing through the line properly. Test strips were getting 0ppm. Kitchen Manager is going to have the chemical moved to a different dispenser in the chemical/dish room. The dispenser at the 3 part sink has been an issue off and on. Today sani-tabs were used for buckets, but sometimes the chemical from the dispenser is used. Do not use the wall dispenser for filling sanitizer buckets until it has been repaired and is dispensing properly or the chemical has been moved to another unit that can dispense the solution at proper concentration of 200ppm.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) bottom inside warmer; B) bulk sugar and flour storage bins; C) counter under microwave; D) tray on lower shelf of prep table holding cutting board rack and box of plastic wrap; E) top surface of metal table next to can rack in dry storage room; F) walkin cooler shelves (mold & splash); & G) front service line storage shelves. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. **Kitchen Manager cleaned the front service line storage shelves during the inspection**

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - A) Single service sandwich boxes were observed food surface up at two different locations. One set of sandwich boxes also had food splash on the side of containers. B) Single service plates were sitting with food surface of top plate in direct contact with the packaging of a Ritz Bitz box. C) Single service utensils were observed in a bus tub with food contact surfaces an handles intermixed. Management was advised gloves must be worn when bulk single service utensils are sorted and placed on trays due to food surfaces and handles being intermixed in order to avoid unnecessary bare hand contact with food surfaces. D) Shelf at front line used for storage of single service containers was observed to be dusty and have some food debris on it. Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects food surfaces from potential contamination. Maintain storage areas clean and store boxes and plates inverted and away from general surfaces that are not clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor below sink at prep table had water on it and was soiled. Clean the floor and eliminate pudding water. B) Gaps were observed along top of stainless steel coving around the wall by the fryers. Re-seal the tops of the coving to the wall. C) A section of tile behind the men's room door was damaged where an old floor stop has been removed. Fill in gaps and repair the tiles so they are smooth, easily cleanable, and do not provide a potential hiding place for pests. Floors shall be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) Lower ledge of dish tray return window was rusty on the surface and had a rubber seal at the bottom that was pulling apart and had black mold buildup in crevices. Removed damaged rubber seal and clean/resurface the ledge. B) Seams along outside of walkin coolers and freezer had silicone/rubber seals that were starting to get moldy and pull apart in some spots. Clean and reseal the seams on the outside of the walkin units. Walls and attached equipment shall be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Potentially hazardous foods (PHF) prepared w/in the last few days stored in walkin cooler #2 had internal temperatures 45F-49F (see general comments for complete list). All foods that were prepared between 5/12 & 5/15 and were above 41F were discarded. Bacon slices on trays that were laid out earlier this morning had surface temperatures of 48F-49 and were also discarded. All other foods that were able to be kept (frozen, marinating chicken, fruit, vegetables, soup base, etc.) were moved to walkin cooler #1, which was holding at 41F/below. Cold PHF must be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Walkin cooler #2 was not holding at 41F/below. External thermostat was reading at 47F, and internal thermometer was at 49F. Foods were discarded or kept and moved to walkin cooler #1 dependent upon temperatures of products (see #3a for details). Call for service was made to Henson Robinson during the inspection, and a repair person arrived during the inspection. Cooler had a bad fan motor, and it will be replaced first thing tomorrow morning. All refrigeration units used to store PHF shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Aluminum foil was observed lining the spice storage shelf in the prep area. A greasy buildup was present under the foil. Remove the aluminum foil and maintain the shelf clean. B) Base of handles at prep sink across from oven had slight gaps and plumbing was loose. Water was seeping through and getting on the shelf below where clean cutting boards were stored. Provide proper seal around the base of the prep sink handles. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Chlorine test strips are not available for checking solutions of bleach water. Inspector's test strips were used to verify solution was at proper concentration (100ppm) when bleach water for in place cleaning of slicer was made. Maintain a supply of chlorine test strips on-site. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750.830f - A plate in clean storage area had food debris stuck to it. Plate was removed and taken to dish room to go through ware washing process again. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine. Repeat the process as many times as needed to ensure all items are properly cleaned and sanitized. Do not store soiled equipment/utensils with clean items.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.820 & 800b - Quat solution was not dispensing properly from the wall unit, and sanitizer buckets were made using that solution. Employee was observed  wiping down the slicer upon arrival of inspector. Bleach solution was made (100ppm) and slicer was cleaned/sanitized again. Bucket for general surfaces at 2 part prep sink was re-made using Steramine tablets (200ppm). Call for service was made to GFS to come out for the Quat wall dispenser. The solution from the wall dispenser will not be used until it has been repaired and is working properly. Use Steramine tabs for making sanitizer solutions, and follow the instructions to ensure tablets dissolve properly to allow for proper sanitizing of surfaces.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Solution for wiping general surfaces was at 0ppm quat. Solution was remade with Steramine tabs at proper concentration of 200ppm. Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200ppm quat. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions or wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) slicer (see #20a); B) can opener (dried food debris); C) plate (see #18); & D) cutting boards (see #15 & #24). Properly wash, rinse, and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use utensils such as can openers, knives, etc., must be switched out up to every 4 hrs.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - A) Soiled plate was observed stored in a stack with clean plates (see #18). Plate was removed and taken to dish room. B) Shelf holding cutting boards had puddling water on it (see #15 part B). Cleaned and sanitized equipment/utensils shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Keep storage areas clean, and do not store soiled equipment with clean items.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Steramine tabs in sanitizer buckets were not dissolving properly, and solutions were testing at about 100ppm quat. Solutions were just made prior to arrival of inspector, but tabs were still not dissolved after an hour of walking around the facility. Manager discarded all solutions and used wall dispenser to remake solutions. Sanitizer solutions were at 200ppm after being remade. Maintain sanitizing solutions at 200ppm quat. Be sure to follow label directions on tablets and use warm water for solutions made with Steramine tabs.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) dry storage room - lower rungs of rolling shelves & table next to #10 can rack; B) shelves in walkin freezer below fan (ice accumulation); C) shelves in walkin cooler #2 (debris/mold); D) milk storage shelves in walkin cooler #1 (milk splash); E) dish machine - curtains and surfaces immediately around curtains on dirty dish side, legs and general surfaces around mechanicals beneath the machine (lime/dust/splash)h; F) bottom legs/rung of steamer (splash); & G) inside panels of fryers (grease/food debris). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. **Manager cleaned shelves in walkin cooler during the inspection**

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

A stack of paper towels from a different dispenser were placed at the handsink until the dispenser could be fixed. Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing at all times.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.(CORRECTED)Removed chemical bottle and put with other chemicals in the dish room.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:

750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the hot water faucet leaking in the men's restroom sink.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
(CORRECTED) Observed white Styrofoam cup stored in the flour bulk bin. White cup was removed.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present

Absence of certified food service manager at this establishment at this time. Class has been taken and awaiting results.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

Flat of eggs stored above ready to eat ham in the walkin cooler.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.
